articles.name: ask-for-intro.md
articles.text:
---
title: Ask for the introduction
dek: Prospektor writes both emails: your ask to the person you know, and the one they can send on for you.
topic: warm
order: 3
next: warm-intros, say-what-happened
---

## How to do it

1. Find the path to the company in **Warm intros**, or open the **Warm paths** card on a finished pitch.
2. Under the best path, read the two drafts: the ask you send the person you know, and the finished email they can send on to the company.
3. Press **Open in Mail** to open your own mail app with the ask filled in, then add their address. Or press **Copy** on either draft.
4. Fill in anything left in [brackets] before you send.
5. Once you have asked, press the chip that says where it stands: **Asked**, **They said yes**, **No** or **Meeting booked**.

## Good to know

- Prospektor sends nothing and doesn’t hold your contact’s address.
- The ask is short and gives them an easy way to say no.
- **Meeting booked** opens **Outcomes** with the company filled in, so you can note what happened.
- Press a lit chip again to clear it.

articles.name: billing.md
articles.text:
---
title: Billing, pausing and cancelling
dek: Pause for a quiet quarter and keep everything, or cancel. The workspace owner does both from Settings.
topic: account
order: 4
next: your-data, invite-team
---

## How to do it

1. Open **Settings**, then **Plan**. Only the person who owns the workspace can use it.
2. Pick the answer that fits the one question we ask. The buttons stay grey until you do.
3. Press **Pause the subscription** to stop the bill and keep everything, or **Cancel it instead** to end it.
4. To come back after a pause, press **Resume the subscription** on the screen you see when you sign in.
5. To change your card or download invoices, press **Manage billing in Stripe** on the same page.

## Good to know

- The subscription is $999 a month per workspace, paid through Stripe. Prospektor never holds your card details.
- Cancelling does not delete your work, and deleting the workspace does not cancel the bill.
- Refunds and billing questions are answered by a person over email.
- If an agency set up your workspace, ask them. The **Plan** page says so.

articles.name: call-recordings.md
articles.text:
---
title: Teach it from your call recordings
dek: Your recorded calls hold the objections you keep hearing. Prospektor reads them and offers the lines worth keeping.
topic: sharper
order: 2
next: say-what-happened, ideal-customer, prep-a-call
---

## How to do it

1. Export a few call transcripts as text from whatever records your calls (Fathom, Otter, Granola or Zoom all can).
2. Open **Settings**, then **Outcomes**.
3. Press **Bring your call recordings** and pick up to six files.
4. Read what comes back: the objections people raised, the questions they asked and the answers that landed. Each line names the calls it came from.
5. Press **Keep** on the lines you agree with. They go into **Your brief**, the description of your company that every pitch, call sheet and reply is written from. Press × to drop a line.

## Good to know

- It works in your first week, before any deal has closed.
- A text file works (.txt, .md, .vtt or .srt). A PDF or a Word document is not read.
- Each transcript is read once and then thrown away. Only the lines it wrote and the file’s name are kept.
- An objection that shows up in two calls is listed first.

articles.name: competitors-customers.md
articles.text:
---
title: Find a competitor’s customers
dek: They already pay for what you sell. Prospektor finds who they are and writes your first email to one of them.
topic: who
order: 4
next: glance, make-it-yours
---

## How to do it

1. Open **Counterprospekt** in the menu on the left. Each competitor has a card, and the ones you already told Prospektor about are there.
2. Press **Find their clients** on one of them. Missing a competitor? Type its name or website in the last card, **Add a competitor**, and press **Find their clients** there.
3. Their clients land in one table, **Leads from your competitors**, best fit first. Each one links the page that names it, so you can check.
4. Press **Glance** on the client you most want to win. About fifteen seconds later you get a fit score out of 100 and the reason.
5. Press **Write the pitch** on that row. A few minutes later the pitch is in your **Library**, with emails in your voice, ready to edit and send.

## Good to know

- A company is listed only when a page Prospektor read says it is their client. Nothing is guessed.
- Each report also names their strength, their weakness and how you win.
- Wrong rival? Open its report with **See their clients ›** and press **Not a competitor**. It leaves the list.
- A client on your **Do not contact** list shows with no pitch button.

articles.name: connect-apps.md
articles.text:
---
title: Connect your CRM, Slack or Claude
dek: Send finished pitches into your CRM, post them to a Slack channel, or let your own Claude do the work for you.
topic: account
order: 2
next: share-a-pitch, invite-team, billing
---

## How to do it

1. Open **Settings**, then **Connectors**. Each app has a tile that says whether it is connected.
2. For a CRM, press its tile. HubSpot and Close ask you to approve Prospektor on their own screen. The others ask you to paste a key from your CRM and press **Connect**.
3. For Slack, press **Connect Slack** and pick the channel, or paste the webhook address Slack gives you and press **Connect**. Every finished pitch then posts a short note there.
4. For Claude or ChatGPT, press its tile, then **Copy the address**. Add that address as a custom connector in Claude or ChatGPT.
5. With a CRM connected, a finished pitch has a Push to button named after your CRM, beside **Share**.

## Good to know

- Only the workspace owner sees these settings.
- One CRM at a time. Pushing the same pitch again updates the record instead of adding a second one.
- **Disconnect** stops an app at once. What it already sent stays in that app.
- Missing an app? Press **Request an integration** and name it.

articles.name: decision-makers.md
articles.text:
---
title: Find the people who decide
dek: Name a company and the role you sell to. About a minute later you have the people, with their LinkedIn and work email.
topic: who
order: 5
image: screen-decision-makers.png
next: warm-intros, write-a-pitch, share-a-pitch
---

## How to do it

1. Open **Decision-makers** in the menu on the left.
2. Type the company’s name or website in the first box. In the second, type the role you want, like CFO or Head of Partnerships, or leave it empty for the roles that matter most.
3. Press **Find people**. About a minute later they appear in a table, each with their LinkedIn and a work email when one was found.
4. Need a number? Press **phone?** beside a person.
5. Tick the people you want and press **Download as CSV**, or press **Write the pitch ›** to get the pitch for that company.

## Good to know

- To look up one person, type their name or paste their LinkedIn address in the second box.
- **Same roles at similar companies** looks for the same roles at up to three companies like this one.
- A person is named only when a source backs it. A role nobody could be found for stays a role.
- Nobody on your **Do not contact** list is ever returned.

articles.name: do-not-contact.md
articles.text:
---
title: Keep a company off your list
dek: Name the customers, competitors and people you never want approached. Prospektor stops before it spends anything on them.
topic: account
order: 3
next: ideal-customer, leads-for-you
---

## How to do it

1. Open **Settings**, then **Do not contact**.
2. To rule out a kind of company, write one rule per line under **Standing rules**, such as “Mostly remote workforce”. Press **Save**.
3. To rule out one company or person, press **Add a company or person**.
4. Choose **A company** or **A person**, say why (**Existing customer**, **Competitor**, **Asked not to be approached** or **Other**) and fill in the name. Add the website too, since that is what matches.
5. Press **Add to the list**.

## Good to know

- A company on the list never shows up as a lead, and a pitch on it is refused before it starts.
- A person on the list is left out of the emails, but their company can still be pitched.
- Customers you name on **Ideal customer** are added for you.
- Each entry shows who added it and when. Anyone in the workspace can remove one.

articles.name: get-started.md
articles.text:
---
title: Get started in fifteen minutes
dek: Sign up, see the companies Prospektor found for you, and leave with a first email you would send.
topic: start
order: 1
image: step-01.png
next: leads-for-you, glance, make-it-yours
---

## How to do it

1. On the sign-up page, sign in with Google or your work email.
2. Type your company’s website and say in one sentence what Prospektor should find for you. Pick monthly or yearly and pay on Stripe.
3. You land on **Home**. While Prospektor reads your website, it asks who already buys from you. Answer it or leave it. About a minute later your first three leads appear.
4. Press **Glance** on the top lead. About fifteen seconds later you see how well it fits and why.
5. Press **Prospekt →**. The pitch takes a few minutes and lands in your **Library**, so you can do something else meanwhile.
6. Open the pitch and its email sequence, press the pencil, rewrite it until you would send it, and press **Save**.

## Good to know

- A saved edit teaches Prospektor how you write. An edit you copy out without saving teaches it nothing.
- **Your brief**, under **Settings**, is the description of your company Prospektor writes from. Fix anything wrong there.
- Anyone with an email at your company’s domain can sign in after you.

articles.name: glance.md
articles.text:
---
title: Glance at a company before you spend a pitch
dek: Fifteen seconds tells you whether a company is worth a full pitch, and who to approach there.
topic: who
order: 2
next: write-a-pitch, decision-makers, research-a-company
---

## How to do it

1. Press **Glance** on any company Prospektor shows you, on **Leads for you** or in a competitor’s client list. On **Research**, type a name and press **Glance →**.
2. Wait about fifteen seconds. You get a fit score out of 100, the one reason it fits, a few signals for and against, and the roles worth approaching.
3. Want names? Press **Name the people →**. About a minute later the roles become named people, each with a source.
4. Like what you see? Press **Prospekt →** for the full pitch. It takes a few minutes and lands in your **Library**.
5. Need one piece only? Under **What to send**, press the one you want, such as a deck or a one-pager. It arrives in under 90 seconds.

## Good to know

- Every glance is kept in your **Library**, marked **Glance**.
- When a company runs more than one line of business, the glance says which one it scored.
- Know something Prospektor doesn’t? On **Research**, add a note under **More options ›** before you press **Glance →**. The glance says what it made of your note.

articles.name: ideal-customer.md
articles.text:
---
title: Tell it who your ideal customer is
dek: Seven short answers decide which companies Prospektor goes looking for. The better they are, the better your leads.
topic: sharper
order: 3
image: screen-settings.png
next: leads-for-you, do-not-contact, lookalikes
---

## How to do it

1. Open **Settings**, then **Ideal customer**.
2. Answer the question on screen in your own words and press **Next**. Press **Skip** to come back to one later.
3. Once most are answered, you see the list. A row marked **Missing**, **Check** or **Add more** wants your attention. **Check** means Prospektor guessed it from your website.
4. Press any row to change that answer.
5. Press **Sharpen the hunt** to rate five companies yes or no. Your answers teach it where a good lead ends.

## Good to know

- Customers you name here are never approached. They join your do not contact list as you save.
- Name your competitors and Prospektor hunts among their customers instead of suggesting the competitors to you.
- Where and how big take plain words, like “DACH” or “startups under 50”.
- Every new search for leads reads these answers.

articles.name: import-network.md
articles.text:
---
title: Bring in who you know from LinkedIn
dek: Add the people you know once, and every company you look at shows who could introduce you.
topic: warm
order: 1
next: warm-intros, ask-for-intro
---

## How to do it

1. Open **Warm intros** in the menu on the left. The first time, it is one box.
2. The quickest way: type who you know, one per line, with how you know them after a comma. Press **Add them**.
3. For all your LinkedIn connections, press **Import a LinkedIn export**. On LinkedIn, go to Settings & Privacy, then Data privacy, then Get a copy of your data. Tick Connections and press Request archive.
4. LinkedIn emails you a download link, usually within ten minutes. Unzip it, choose Connections.csv and press **Import the file**.
5. On the **Your network** tab, mark the people who will help as **Always introduces** or **Might introduce**. Add more lists with **Add people ›**.

## Good to know

- Email addresses in the export are dropped and never stored.
- Each teammate imports their own connections. Only the person who brought an import can remove it.
- Uploading a newer export updates your list without counting anyone twice.
- Gmail or Outlook contacts come in through **Import an address book**.

articles.name: inbound.md
articles.text:
---
title: Answer an inbound lead
dek: Paste what a lead sent you and get the reply to send, in your voice, plus whether they are worth your time.
topic: what
order: 5
next: prep-a-call, make-it-yours
---

## How to do it

1. Open **Inbound** in the menu on the left. It opens on **Reply**.
2. Paste what they sent as it is: the email, the LinkedIn message or the form.
3. If you like, press **More options** to add their company and anything the reply must say, such as your price or when you can start.
4. Press **Write the reply**. Within a minute you see **Worth answering** or **Skip it**, and the reply under it.
5. Press **Copy the reply** and send it from your own mail.
6. If they are worth a call, press **Prepare the call** for a call sheet.

## Good to know

- It never makes up a price, a date or a promise. A number in the reply comes only from what you typed under **More options**.
- When a quote needs facts the message doesn’t give, **Ask before you quote** lists what to find out first.
- **Why** shows who sent it and what they really want.
- Your replies are kept under **Recent** on the same screen.

articles.name: invite-team.md
articles.text:
---
title: Invite your team
dek: Add a colleague by email and they get a sign-in link. They can pitch, prep calls and edit from day one.
topic: account
order: 1
next: connect-apps, import-network, billing
---

## How to do it

1. Open **Settings**, then **Team**.
2. Type their email address in the box at the top.
3. Choose **member** or **admin**.
4. Press **Invite**. They are added and get an email with a sign-in link.
5. Beside each name you see whether they have joined. If the email never arrived, send it again with the invite link on their row.

## Good to know

- Only an owner or an admin can add people. A member does all the sales work; an admin also manages people and settings.
- Only the owner can change roles or delete the workspace.
- Removing someone takes effect at once. There are no passwords: people sign in with Google or a link sent by email.
- An entry that starts with @ lets everyone at that domain sign in, and sends no email.

articles.name: leads-for-you.md
articles.text:
---
title: See the leads Prospektor found for you
dek: Companies that fit what you sell, waiting when you open the studio. Check any of them in fifteen seconds.
topic: who
order: 1
image: step-02.png
next: glance, lookalikes, competitors-customers
---

## How to do it

1. Open **Leads for you** in the menu on the left. Each card shows a fit score out of 100, the company, its website and the one thing that makes it worth a look.
2. Press **Glance** on the card you like best. About fifteen seconds later you see why it fits and which roles to approach.
3. Wrong company? Press the **×** and pick **Not a fit**, or **Our client** if they already buy from you. Another card takes its place.
4. Want a different kind of company? Press one of the lines under the cards, such as **are hiring**. The new leads arrive in a row headed by what you pressed.

## Good to know

- Each row says why it is there, such as a customer you named or a deal you closed.
- **Our client** puts the company on **Do not contact**, and the next search looks for more like it.
- A company leaves this list once you glance at it, pitch it or remove it. Anything you glanced stays in your **Library**.
- The top three leads also show on **Home**.

articles.name: lookalikes.md
articles.text:
---
title: Find companies like your best customer
dek: Name the customers you already have. Prospektor finds more companies like them and adds them to your leads.
topic: who
order: 3
next: leads-for-you, glance, ideal-customer
---

## How to do it

1. Open **Research** in the menu on the left and pick the **Lookalikes** tab.
2. Under **Customers you already have**, type one customer per line. Customers you named before are already there.
3. After each name, add why they are a good customer, like “they already had the drivers”. That tells Prospektor what to look for in similar companies.
4. Press **Find more like these**. You go straight to **Leads for you**, where the new companies arrive as cards.
5. Press **Glance** on one to see how it fits, then **Prospekt →** for the pitch.

## Good to know

- The new leads sit in a row named after the customer they resemble.
- The customers you name are saved with your answers on **Ideal customer**.
- You can also type “companies like” and a name in the bar at the top of **Home**.

articles.name: make-it-yours.md
articles.text:
---
title: Make the email sound like you
dek: Rewrite one email the way you’d send it, save it, and every pitch after that is written closer to how you write.
topic: what
order: 2
next: write-a-pitch, ideal-customer
---

## How to do it

1. Open a finished pitch from your **Library** and stay on **The pitch**.
2. Press the pencil on the part you want to change.
3. Rewrite it until you would send it as it is.
4. Press **Save & teach**. The next pitch starts from what you saved.
5. To set your tone for everything at once, open **Settings**, then **Your brief** (the description of your company that Prospektor writes from). Your tone is under **How you sound**. Press **Edit** to change it.

## Good to know

- Saved edits teach tone and structure only. Facts from one company never show up in another company’s email.
- An edit you copy out without saving teaches it nothing.
- Each new pitch draws on the saved edits closest to the company it is writing for, so the fiftieth edit still counts.
- Once you save your brief yourself, Prospektor stops changing it.

articles.name: not-working.md
articles.text:
---
title: When something is not working
dek: What to press when a pitch fails, and how to tell us when that does not fix it.
topic: account
order: 6
next: your-data, invite-team, get-started
---

## How to do it

1. If a pitch failed, press **Rerun**. It starts again on the same company.
2. If it fails again, press **Share this bug with Prospektor**. That sends us what went wrong on that pitch.
3. For anything else, press **Help** and ask the support chat in your own words.
4. If the studio says it is reconnecting, wait. It opens by itself when it can, and **Status** shows whether it is only you.

## Good to know

- A pitch that runs past fifteen minutes is marked as not finished, with **Rerun** beside it.
- If a colleague cannot sign in, their address is probably missing from **Team**.
- If a shared link says it is not available, the workspace is paused. Resuming brings every link back.
- When a bug you shared leads to a fix, your workspace gets one pitch on us.

articles.name: prep-a-call.md
articles.text:
---
title: Prepare for a call
dek: One sheet for the call you are about to take: the goal, what to say, what to ask, and the answer to their likely pushback.
topic: what
order: 4
image: screen-meeting-prep.png
next: inbound, say-what-happened
---

## How to do it

1. Open **Inbound** in the menu on the left and press **Prepare a call**. On a finished pitch, **Prep a call** in the ⋯ menu opens it with the company filled in.
2. Type the company or its website.
3. Pick which call it is: **First call**, **Discovery / follow-up**, **Pitch / proposal**, **Negotiation / closing** or **Kickoff / check-in**.
4. If you like, press **More options** and add a note about the call.
5. Press **Prep me**. The sheet holds the goal, how to frame it, what to say, what to ask, the pushback with an answer, and how to close.
6. Press **Copy the sheet** to keep it as plain text.

## Good to know

- With a pitch already written for the company, the sheet uses its research and lands in under a minute.
- Your sheets are kept under **Recent preps** on the same screen.
- You can leave the screen while it works.

articles.name: research-a-company.md
articles.text:
---
title: Look up one company you have in mind
dek: Type a name and know in fifteen seconds whether it fits. One more press gets you the full pitch.
topic: who
order: 6
next: glance, write-a-pitch, decision-makers
---

## How to do it

1. Press **Prospekt a company** at the top of the menu on the left, or open **Research**. Stay on the **One company** tab.
2. Type the company’s name or website, and pick the right one from the list as you type.
3. Know something about them? Open **More options ›** and add a note, such as a deadline or someone you know there.
4. Press **Glance →**. In about fifteen seconds you see the fit, the one reason and the roles to approach.
5. Want the full pitch? Press **Prospekt**. It takes a few minutes and lands in your **Library**.

## Good to know

- Prospektor tells you when your team has already pitched that company.
- Paste a company’s website into the bar on **Home** and this screen opens with the company filled in.
- You can leave while a pitch is written. It keeps going without you.
- Got many companies? The **A whole list** tab takes them all at once.

articles.name: say-what-happened.md
articles.text:
---
title: Say what happened after you sent it
dek: One press tells Prospektor how a pitch went, and every pitch after it is written with that in mind.
topic: sharper
order: 1
next: call-recordings, ideal-customer, write-a-pitch
---

## How to do it

1. Find the company in your **Library**, or open its finished pitch. Its badge reads **What happened?** until you set it.
2. Press the badge and pick how far it got: **Found the right contact**, **Had a meeting** or **Closed the deal**.
3. If it ended, pick how instead: **Went quiet**, **Not a fit** or **Lost**.
4. To add their reply or your call notes, open **Settings**, then **Outcomes**. Type the company, pick what happened, paste the text and press **Save it**.
5. While a deal is still open, the button reads **Save and say what’s next**. It saves your notes and suggests the next step, with the message to send.

## Good to know

- Two weeks after a pitch, Home asks what happened with that company. One press answers it.
- You can record any company, including a deal Prospektor never found for you.
- Your notes shape what Prospektor writes next. They are never quoted in an email it drafts.
- With a CRM connected, **Outcomes** can bring in the deals you already won in one go.

articles.name: send-a-deck.md
articles.text:
---
title: Send a deck with your email
dek: Get a short pitch deck about this company, in your colours, ready to attach or share as a link.
topic: what
order: 3
image: screen-pitch-deck.png
next: write-a-pitch, share-a-pitch
---

## How to do it

1. Open a finished pitch. At the top of **The pitch**, press the menu that shows the format you are on, and pick **Pitch deck**.
2. Press **Write the pitch deck →**. It lands on the same tab in about a minute.
3. The first time, it asks what your decks should be built from: **Write a standing deck →**, **Upload a reference** (a deck you already send) or **No template**. You answer once.
4. Fix any slide with its pencil button.
5. Press **Download .pptx** and attach the file to your email. Or press **Share** on the deck for a link to the deck alone.

## Good to know

- With a standing deck, every pitch reuses your slides and adds one slide about the company, with no wait.
- Change the answer or edit your standing deck in **Settings**, then **Brand**.
- The last slide carries a small line saying Prospektor researched it, with the date. It can’t be removed.

articles.name: share-a-pitch.md
articles.text:
---
title: Share a pitch or send it to your CRM
dek: Send a colleague or client a link to the pitch, or put the company and its people straight into your CRM.
topic: what
order: 6
next: connect-apps, invite-team
---

## How to do it

1. Open a finished pitch from your **Library**.
2. Press **Share** at the top to share the whole pitch. To send one document, like the deck, press **Share** on that document instead.
3. Press **Copy link** and send it however you like.
4. To send it to your CRM, open the ⋯ menu at the top and press **Push to** followed by your CRM’s name. You first see everything it would write.
5. Press **Write it to** your CRM to send it.

## Good to know

- Whoever opens a link signs up first. They see that one pitch and nothing else in your workspace.
- A link to one document carries none of the research behind it.
- **Revoke** any link in **Settings**, then **Sharing**. It stops working at once, even for someone who already opened it.
- Pushing the same pitch again updates the records in your CRM instead of making new ones. The workspace owner connects the CRM in **Settings**, then **Connectors**.

articles.name: warm-intros.md
articles.text:
---
title: Find who can introduce you
dek: Type a company and see who in your network can get you in, and why they would.
topic: warm
order: 2
next: ask-for-intro, import-network
---

## How to do it

1. Open **Warm intros** in the menu on the left, on the **Introductions** tab.
2. Type a company into the box. Before you press anything, it shows who you already know there.
3. Press **Find the path**. You get how many paths it found, the best one first with why it works, and the rest folded under it.
4. The best path comes with the emails to ask for the introduction, ready to send.
5. Lower on the screen, **Introductions to pursue** lists companies from **Leads for you** and your **Library** that someone you know can reach. Press **Pursue it** on one.

## Good to know

- It needs your network first. Bring it in from **Warm intros** before you search.
- A finished pitch shows the same thing in a **Warm paths** card under **Who to write to**, with a **Way in** column naming who reaches each person.
- Finding nothing is a normal answer, and it says which people it checked.
- People you mark as **Always introduces** come first.

articles.name: write-a-pitch.md
articles.text:
---
title: Get a pitch written for one company
dek: Name a company and get the emails to send the people who decide there, written in your voice.
topic: what
order: 1
image: screen-cold-email.png
next: make-it-yours, send-a-deck, share-a-pitch
---

## How to do it

1. Press **Prospekt a company** at the top of the menu on the left.
2. Type the company’s name or website and press **Glance →**. In about fifteen seconds you see how well they fit, the one reason to write, and the roles worth calling.
3. Under **What to send**, press **Sequence** to get the emails. Or press **Prospekt →** to research deeper and write everything at once (a few minutes).
4. The pitch opens on **The pitch**. Each person gets their own emails: press a name to switch.
5. Press **Copy** and paste the email into your own mail, or press **Download CSV** to import the whole sequence into the tool you send with.

## Good to know

- Prospektor writes the emails and you send them. Nothing goes out on its own.
- Anything in [brackets] is something it would not guess. Fill it in before you send.
- Some steps are LinkedIn messages. Paste those into LinkedIn yourself.
- You can leave while it works. The pitch waits in your **Library**.

articles.name: your-data.md
articles.text:
---

## How to do it

1. To see who can open your work, open **Settings**, then **Team**. Only the people listed there can.
2. To see what the studio keeps in your browser, press **Cookies** at the foot of any page.
3. To remove a company you recorded by mistake, open it from **Outcomes** and press **Remove this record**.
4. To remove everything, the owner opens **Settings**, then **Profile**, and uses **Delete workspace** in the **Danger zone**. There is no undo.

## Good to know

- Nothing is deleted on its own. Your work stays until someone in your workspace deletes it.
- Prospektor staff see counts and dates about your workspace, never your pitches. Support chats and feature requests you send are read by the team.
- What you record about your deals shapes what Prospektor writes, and is never quoted in an email it drafts.
- The privacy policy on prospektor.ai has the full detail.
